cells.tense: What was imagined has been felt fully and the feeling has landed here.
cells.act: move at the pace your feeling can sustain
cells.ask: Let the pace you keep this week be one your feeling can actually carry. Not the pace a strong week allows. Steady enough that an ordinary month would not wreck it.
cells.core:
Something you imagined has been felt all the way through, and that is what completion is. Not because everything is perfect — because what was in you has been lived, and the living satisfied it. Care for what is growing works from exactly here. You tend without forcing, and the growing responds because the conditions are right.

Let the pace you keep this week be one your feeling can actually carry. Not the pace a strong week allows, but the one that would fit if the month turned plain. Peaceful momentum is what a steady pace is like when you are in it. The next piece gets easier to hold when this one is not rushed toward finishing faster than it can arrive.
cells.sheetLine: What you imagined has been felt — that is the completion.
cells.verb: arriving at the abundant satisfaction of having fully imagined and fully felt
cells.place: where care tends what is growing without forcing the outcome

cells.tense: You are braced at a future that cannot yet be written into the present.
cells.ask: Find the part of what you are growing that you grip — the piece you check several times a day — and tend it weekly instead. Watch what keeps coming up without the grip.
cells.core:
The care has tipped into gripping. What you are growing gets attended before it has had a chance to need attention, and the attention itself starts to feel like pressure — to you and to it. The dream runs ahead of what has actually been lived, so the vision outruns the ground it ought to stand on. That is not failure. It is care that has not yet found its right shape.

Steward it without clutching. Find the piece you check several times a day, then tend it weekly and leave the rest alone between. The growing does not need your hand on it every hour. Let the care be responsible without being constant, and notice which parts keep coming up anyway. Those are held by something other than worry, and those are the ones worth your steady hand.
cells.sheetLine: Care that clutches is care that has not found its shape.

cells.tense: You are still standing at a door that closed behind you.
cells.act: hold two true things without declaring either
cells.ask: Set two things you have not been able to choose between on one page, and carry both without picking. Notice which one you keep coming back to.
cells.core:
What you imagined did not get felt all the way through. Some of it stayed imagined, and the door you stood at is behind you now. The care for what is growing is still in you, but it has gone quiet — not much is being tended, and the not-tending has started to feel like a fact about you rather than a season. The feeling does not need forcing back. What you see needs to land again.

Set two things you cannot choose between on one page and carry both without picking. Comfort with not-deciding is not indecision — it is the ground decisions come from when they are ready. If nothing moves, the waiting still gives you something: the one you kept returning to. That one has already decided itself. You just have not heard it yet.

cells.tense: You are steering without noticing your hands are on the wheel.
cells.act: refine one distinction by close attention
cells.ask: Choose something you tend and tell apart what actually helps it grow from what only looks like helping. Watch it without changing a thing yet.
cells.core:
The care for what is growing keeps going, and your account of yourself is that you are not really tending anything. But things near you keep coming up, and you keep being the reason. That is a hand on the wheel you have not been willing to name. The telling-apart is already happening — you can see what matters from what does not — it just isn't owned by you yet.

Choose something you tend and tell apart what actually helps it grow from what only looks like helping. Do not act on the difference yet. Watch it without changing anything, the way you would watch a plant to see which way it leans. The distinction is the practice. It connects you to the work without asking you to admit you are doing it. That admission can come later, when the evidence has stacked itself.
cells.sheetLine: You are already tending it — practice noticing what you know.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is that 'what you imagined has been felt' maps onto something already complete in the person's life; readers may object that satisfaction in the making is not the same as satisfaction in the outcome. The sentence that serves me more than them is any line that names feeling as a commodity; I write around it.
